skill.name: ubiquitous-language
skill.description: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation, flag ambiguities, propose canonical terms, and save the result to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.
skill.summary: Creates a domain-driven design glossary from conversation context and updates it as terminology evolves.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Domain teams often use conflicting words for the same concept. This skill extracts terms from discussion and saves a canonical glossary with ambiguities flagged.
actual_capabilities: Scans the current conversation for domain-relevant nouns, verbs, and concepts.
Identifies ambiguous terms, synonyms, and overloaded wording.
Proposes canonical terms with definitions and aliases to avoid.
Groups related terms into markdown tables by domain area.
Writes the glossary to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md in the working directory.
Updates an existing glossary when invoked again in the same conversation.
limitations: Quality depends on the conversation context available to the assistant.
It does not validate terminology against external domain experts.
It writes a markdown file only in the current working directory.
It intentionally skips generic programming terms unless they are domain concepts.

use_cases.title: Clarify Product Terms
use_cases.description: Turn stakeholder discussion into a shared glossary before requirements harden.

use_cases.title: Align Domain Models
use_cases.description: Resolve competing names for entities, actors, and lifecycle states during design work.

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Vocabulary
use_cases.description: Update a project glossary as conversations introduce new terms or change meanings.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use after a planning discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this conversation and create a ubiquitous language glossary for the domain. Save it to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

prompt_templates.title: Find Ambiguous Terms
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use when terminology feels inconsistent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the domain terms from our discussion, flag ambiguous words, and recommend one canonical term for each concept.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use after more discovery work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the existing UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md, add new terms from this conversation, and revise definitions that changed.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Domain Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for DDD modeling sessions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this conversation to group domain terms by subdomain, describe relationships, and write an example dialogue that clarifies boundaries.

output_examples.input: A checkout discussion uses account for both a buyer organization and a login identity.
output_examples.output: The glossary separates Customer from User, defines each term, and flags account as an alias to avoid.

output_examples.input: A fulfillment team discusses orders, shipments, invoices, cancellations, and delivery confirmation.
output_examples.output: The output groups lifecycle terms, explains relationships, and recommends precise names for each business event.

output_examples.input: A project already has a glossary, but a new meeting adds refund and return concepts.
output_examples.output: The skill updates the existing glossary with the new terms and refreshes the example dialogue.

best_practices: Provide real stakeholder discussion before invoking the skill.
Review flagged ambiguities with a domain expert before adopting final terms.
Re-run the skill after major discovery sessions to keep the glossary current.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for domain expert validation.
Do not include implementation jargon unless it has domain meaning.
Do not treat suggested aliases as final without team review.

faq.question: What file does this skill create?
faq.answer: It writes a markdown glossary named UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md in the current working directory.

faq.question: Does it require a specific project type?
faq.answer: No. It works best with any project that has domain language, stakeholders, and evolving requirements.

faq.question: Can it update an existing glossary?
faq.answer: Yes. When invoked again, it reads the existing glossary and incorporates new terms from later discussion.

faq.question: Does it execute code or shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructions focus on conversation analysis and markdown glossary writing.

faq.question: How accurate are the suggested terms?
faq.answer: Accuracy depends on the conversation quality. A domain expert should review final wording.

faq.question: Can it help with domain-driven design?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports DDD work by making shared terminology explicit and consistent.
